title: Duo Authentication Denials
exclusions: Does not cover sign-ins to applications that are not protected by Duo, and does not see password failures that happen before Duo is called. Use the identity provider's sign-in log for those.
evidence: Saved alert results with user, reasons, applications, source IP count, and countries, plus the analyst's disposition (takeover attempt, lost device, or service account).

controlTest.positiveScenario: Sign in to a Duo-protected test application as a test user and deny the Duo Push ten times within an hour. Within one input interval the denials appear in `index=duo` with `result=denied` and `reason=user_mistake` or `no_response`, and the search returns one row for the user with `denials` at 10 or more.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Sign in as the same user, deny twice, and approve the third push. The events are indexed, but the user stays under the threshold and the search returns no row.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Authentication log type, which polls `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication`. One JSON event per authentication or enrollment attempt with `event_type`, `result`, `reason`, `factor`, `user.name`, `application.name`, `access_device.*`, and `auth_device.*`.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="authentication"
| eval result=lower(result), user=coalesce('user.name', username), app_name='application.name', src='access_device.ip', country='access_device.location.country'
| search result IN ("denied", "failure", "fraud")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as denials dc(src) as src_count values(reason) as reasons values(app_name) as applications values(country) as countries by _time user
| where denials >= 10
| sort - denials
description: Counts denied, failed, and fraud-marked Duo authentication attempts per user per hour from the v2 authentication log and flags users with ten or more. Each row lists the Duo reasons, the applications targeted, the source IP count, and the countries seen.
value: A burst of Duo denials for one user means someone has that user's password and is failing the second factor, or the user is locked out of their device. Both need a response within the hour: the first is an account takeover attempt, the second is a service-desk call that is about to happen.
implementation: Collect the Duo Authentication log (v2) with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`. Schedule hourly, alert on users with at least ten denials in an hour, and tune the threshold per application after two weeks.
visualization: Alert table: _time, user, denials, reasons, applications, src_count, countries. Supporting panels: timechart of denials by reason (stacked column), top users by denials over 7 days (bar chart).

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Lost or replaced phones** — a user with a new phone fails Duo Push repeatedly with `no_response` or `no_activated_duo_mobile_account` until the device is re-activated. Check `reasons` before escalating.

2. **Misconfigured service accounts** — scripts that authenticate through a Duo-protected application without a second factor fail every run. They show one application, one source IP, and a steady hourly count.

3. **Policy rollouts** — a new policy that denies an OS version or location produces denials for many users at once with `reason` set to `platform_restricted` or `location_restricted`.

**Suppression:** a lookup of service accounts with an owner, and a 4-hour throttle per user.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Authentication log type (the v2 endpoint, not Authentication Legacy v1) and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2`. `result` is one of `success`, `denied`, `failure`, `error`, or `fraud` in lowercase; the legacy v1 type `cisco:duo:authentication` uses uppercase values, so the searches lowercase `result` before comparing.
• Device-posture fields under `access_device` (`is_encryption_enabled`, `is_firewall_enabled`, `is_password_set`, `security_agents`) are filled only when the application uses the Duo Universal Prompt and Duo Desktop is installed, and only on Duo Premier or Advantage plans.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 event_type=authentication | stats count by result reason` over 7 days and confirm both fields are populated.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="authentication"
| eval result=lower(result), user=coalesce('user.name', username), app_name='application.name', src='access_device.ip', country='access_device.location.country'
| search result IN ("denied", "failure", "fraud")
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as denials dc(src) as src_count values(reason) as reasons values(app_name) as applications values(country) as countries by _time user
| where denials >= 10
| sort - denials
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line limits the search to authentication attempts; enrollment events share the log but have no `reason`.
• `eval` lowercases `result` so the search also works if any v1 events are still present, and copies the nested JSON fields into short names.
• `denied`, `failure`, and `fraud` are the Duo results that mean the attempt did not get in; `error` is left out because it is usually a Duo-side or network fault.
• `stats` per user per hour keeps the reasons and applications on the row, so the analyst can tell a takeover attempt from a lost phone without another search.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Authentication Log for the same user and time range: each attempt listed there should appear in `index=duo` with the same result and reason.
• Confirm the `reason` values on the alert row match the Reason column in the Admin Panel for at least three attempts.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 | timechart span=1h count by result` over 7 days; gaps longer than two input intervals point to collection failures, not quiet periods.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule hourly over the previous hour and throttle on `user` for 4 hours.
• Route to the identity team. When `reasons` contains `user_marked_fraud` or the countries are unusual for the user, page the SOC instead.
• Review the threshold monthly with the top-users panel; applications with frequent re-prompts may need their own threshold.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
• Searches return nothing but events exist: the input is on Authentication Legacy v1, so events are in `cisco:duo:authentication` with uppercase `result` and flat `username`. Switch the input to the v2 log type rather than editing the searches.
• Missing fields `user.name` or `access_device.ip`: the events were indexed before `KV_MODE=json` applied, or a custom props stanza overrides the add-on. Check `| fieldsummary` on one hour of data.
grandmaExplanation: We count how often each person's second login check fails in an hour, so we notice when someone keeps trying with a stolen password or a person is stuck.
